svg.aria-label: Geologic time scale bar: Precambrian about 88 percent, Paleozoic about 6 percent, Mesozoic about 4 percent, Cenozoic about 1 percent
svg.title: Geologic time scale bar (proportional to duration)
svg.desc: Earth's 4.6-billion-year history as a horizontal bar. Precambrian: 4.6 billion to 539 million years ago, 812 px wide. Paleozoic: 539 to 252 million years ago, 57 px wide. Mesozoic: 252 to 66 million years ago, 37 px wide. Cenozoic: 66 million years ago to today, 14 px wide. Widths are proportional to duration; 1 px is about 5 million years. Period and epoch names are not shown, per the MS-ESS1-4 assessment boundary.
svg.text: Geologic time scale — Earth's 4.6-billion-year history (not to scale vertically; bar widths are proportional to duration)
Paleozoic: 539 – 252 million years ago (~6%) · first fish, first insects, first land animals
Mesozoic: 252 – 66 million years ago (~4%) · first dinosaurs, first mammals, first birds
Cenozoic: 66 million years ago – today (~1%) · mammals spread; humans appear at the very end
Oldest on the left, youngest on the right. Human history is the last 3 millimetres of the 4.6-metre rope in Lesson 05.
